locations.literal: 1.1 **The polynomials and the class $[P]$.** In $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ the elements $1+q^2$ and $2$ differ (their difference $q^2-1$ is nonzero) while $(1+q^2)|_{q=1}=2$; multiplying by the nonzero class $[D]$ gives distinct classes $[P]=(1+q^2)[D]$ and $2[D]$ in the free $A$-module $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H^\Lambda_{\alpha_0+\alpha_1})$, whose images under the forgetful map $\zeta$ (which satisfies $\zeta(qm)=m$) both equal $2[D]$ [[def-graded-module-and-projective-grothendieck-groups-for-klr-towers]] [F1]. [F1]

locations.literal: 1.4 **The ungraded specialization (4).** The forgetful maps satisfy $\zeta(qm)=m$ and specialize $q$ to $1$ [F3]; a graded composition series of a finite-dimensional graded module specializes to an ungraded composition series with the same multiplicities, and the transported identifications therefore specialize to the ungraded statement that the self-dual projective classes are the canonical basis and the simple classes the dual-canonical basis of the basic module, which is Ariki's ungraded canonical-basis statement [F1, F3]. Combining this specialization with the graded decomposition theorem of this page gives the ungraded decomposition-number statement; that combination is recorded as the pointer in clause (4) and is not used in the present proofs [F3, F4]. [F1, F3, F4]
